A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same A3CG dataset and study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations in Tables 2 and 14, adversarial-learning sensitivity results in Appendix C.4, and qualitative error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, sensitivity study, and error analyses, including their detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: The aspect-action task, ABSA adaptations, contrastive objective, adversarial procedure, and prompting methods remain unchanged. Section 4.2 adds model-selection rationale without changing the methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 2,004 English sustainability statements drawn from 1,679 SGX company reports for 2017–2022, with the same ten categories and seen/unseen evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains all ten supervised configurations and the same four LLM families evaluated in zero-shot and few-shot settings. The added explanations of comparator selection do not change participation.

E3.justification: The full-dataset split, three cross-category folds, sample counts, metrics, model versions, training settings, and demonstration-selection procedures are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix C.

E4.justification: Both retain the same adversarial-strength sensitivity study, t-SNE comparisons, category-recall analysis, and syntactic/pragmatic error examples in Figures 4–7 and Tables 11–13. Reorganizing their discussion adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both Table 2 captions specify averaging few-shot results over five random samplings of demonstrations. No new run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests are introduced.

E6.justification: The reported numerical results and qualitative error findings are unchanged, including appendix tables. For example, Table 2 retains unseen-category average AAA F1 of 47.51 for GRACE and 42.03 for Claude 3.5 Sonnet + FS.

T1.justification: The contrastive-loss expression in Section 4.2 and gradient-reversal equation in Appendix C.4 are unchanged. No new formal definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The dataset contribution, cross-category objective, and central comparative findings remain the same. The expanded conclusion summarizes findings already discussed in v1; both versions distinguish A3CG from definitive greenwashing detection.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 adds a pretraining-based explanation for LLMs' smaller transfer drops and qualifies their usefulness in compute-limited settings with API access. Limitations newly acknowledges omitted smaller-LLM fine-tuning and suggests LoRA as future work.

D1.justification: v1 promises a later dataset, code, and report-source release; v2 supplies a repository address and states these materials are available. Implementation details remain unchanged, although Ethical Considerations still retains future-release wording.

R1.justification: v2 adds Varshney et al. (2025), ClimaEmpact, to support the proposed future direction of adapting smaller language models. The existing related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises introductory wording, explains model groupings, moves Comparison of Model Types from Section 5.1 to 5.5, expands the conclusion, and adds acknowledgements. Most prose and the overall section framework are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives an explanatory caption, Table 1 moves after the dataset-statistics text, and text/table placement changes with reflow. The same seven figures and fourteen tables remain, with their substantive displays preserved.

improvement.justification: Concrete resource-access information, clearer model-selection explanations and discussion order, and the explicit fine-tuning limitation improve usability and transparency. The empirical evidence is unchanged, and the added pretraining explanation is not directly tested. These are useful but limited gains, with a residual inconsistency in release-status wording.
